answer: Admission sells by sealed bid: each identity files one sable-sealed bid into an atlas; only bids above the nadir floor of 50 credits qualify. Winners lock their bid as a bond, losers are refunded, so no farmer parks a thousand free identities. The k-th bid costs 50+7(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 3,546,500, while one honest agent pays 50 once and keeps its seat. A bid-pooling ring collapses when the atlas shows duplicate envelopes and burns them.
